---
title: "Test coverage suggestions"
description: "Claude writes testthat tests; only tests that pass are proposed."
---

`test-coverage-suggest.yml` has Claude review each function together with
its existing tests and write new `testthat` tests where they add value. It
**runs every generated test** and proposes only the ones that pass as a
[suggestion PR](suggestions.qmd).

## What it does

- **Every function is reviewed** — changed ones in a PR, all of them in a
  [sweep](suggestions.qmd#sweeps) — whether it already has tests or not.
- **Up to five new tests per function, only if they add value.** Claude
  names the value of each test — an uncovered code path, error handling,
  an edge case, or a likely regression — and tests without such a reason
  are dropped, as are copies of existing tests. See
  [what gets proposed](suggestions.qmd#what-gets-proposed).
- **Existing tests are never changed** — new tests are only appended, or
  the test file is created. One function per file is assumed.
- **Every test is run** with your package loaded from source before it is
  proposed.

## Tests that could be deleted

Claude also points out existing tests that look redundant, test behaviour
the function no longer has, or assert nothing meaningful — with a reason.
Nothing is deleted: the list appears in the suggestion PR's description,
or as a comment on your PR if no new tests were proposed.

## Failing tests

A generated test that fails is not proposed. Claude classifies why it
failed, from the actual error output, and the workflow reports it:

| Classification | Meaning | Reported as |
|---|---|---|
| `real_bug` | The test is right and found a defect | An issue |
| `bad_test` | The test itself is wrong | A comment on your PR |
| `env_misconfiguration` | The test setup is broken, e.g. a missing package | A comment on your PR |

In a [sweep](suggestions.qmd#sweeps) there is no PR to comment on, so the
last two are listed in the sweep PR's description instead, or in one issue
if no test passed at all.

## DataSHIELD client packages

Client-side functions need a DataSHIELD server. With `datashield: true` and
`datashield-type: client`, tests run against
[DSLite](https://github.com/datashield/DSLite), an in-process server:
an existing DSLite `tests/testthat/setup.R` is reused; otherwise one is
created with one of DSLite's bundled datasets.

::: {.callout-important}
DSLite takes the server functions from the **installed server packages**.
List them (e.g. `dsBase`), together with `DSLite` and `testthat`, in your
`DESCRIPTION` — for example under `Suggests` — so the workflow installs
them. Otherwise every test fails as `env_misconfiguration`.
:::
